entries.1c244e36d073deff: Founded in 1970 in Kisarazu, Chiba Prefecture, it transitioned to a holding company structure in April 2024. It is listed on the Growth Market of the Tokyo Stock Exchange and forms a group of 2 companies in total, consisting of the company and 1 consolidated subsidiary (Wakuwaku Hiroba Co., Ltd.). It had 59 employees on a consolidated basis as of September 30, 2025.
entries.1fe8236333984341: This business provides a sharing service that makes the company group's sales floor space available as a sales venue to regional producers and food manufacturers. It operates direct-sales stores nationwide under the Wakuwaku Hiroba brand, and as of September 30, 2025, it operated 182 stores (153 mall stores and 29 street-front stores). Store operations are handled by consolidated subsidiary Wakuwaku Hiroba Co., Ltd., and the number of registered producers is 33,906. Consolidated operating revenue for the fiscal year ended September 2025 was ¥7,982 million. Its head office is located in Mihama-ku, Chiba, Chiba Prefecture, and as of September 30, 2025, consolidated headcount was 59.
entries.2081762ea137d29a: In the fiscal year ended September 2025, it opened 16 new stores while closing 22 stores, and the number of stores at the end of the period was 182, down from 188 at the end of the previous period.
entries.254dc94727204aaa: While sales amounts in the agricultural production-related business through agricultural product direct sales outlets have grown, it is explained that competition is intensifying as the number of supermarkets developing direct-from-producer vegetable corners is also increasing. The group positions itself as a "direct sales plaza connecting regions" that broadly gathers local foods including not only fresh produce but also bento, prepared dishes, breads and processed products, and is a mid-sized direct sales outlet operating platform with operating revenue of ¥7,982 million and 182 stores nationwide.

entries.b14b308da2069433: Its strength lies in the consignment sales system in which the group does not bear inventory risk for products exhibited by producers. Producers bear no registration fees or deposits and need no capital investment, and can freely decide "when, what, how many, and at what price" to exhibit, so even small producers can use sales floors in malls with customer-drawing power. A supply network of producers around stores (local supply chain) is gradually being formed and store sales tend to accumulate, and store facilities are limited to display tables, refrigerated cases, cash registers and the like, making operations simple and low-cost, which is also a characteristic.
